title: Posters/Broadsides
slide_intent: Teach designers to match information density to viewing behavior. A poster must register quickly, while a broadside can reward a closer reading.
strategic_value: NASA can give public communications immediate impact and still identify their source.
demonstration: A shorter astronaut poster and a taller Weather Satellites piece both use a dominant photograph. The headline and signature remain distinct from the image detail.
practical_value: For a distant first read, test the headline, image and mark as a group. Use the broadside format when the audience will spend time with more information.

content_islands.name: Viewing-distance guidance
content_islands.spec: Place the title and two columns of text above the specimens. State the distinction between the quick poster read and the longer broadside read.

content_islands.name: Astronaut poster
content_islands.spec: Place the astronaut image at left with the headline in its upper-left area and the NASA mark near the bottom.

content_islands.name: Weather satellite example
content_islands.spec: Align the taller piece with the poster at the top. Set its information across the dark upper area and use the storm image as the dominant field.
